item.title: Diagens Tech expands medical imaging foundational model platform across specialties
item.description:
Diagens Tech expands medical imaging foundational model platform across specialties

Diagens Tech is extending its medical‑imaging foundational model platform beyond a single regulated use case, allowing clinicians to build, deploy and run thousands of custom models across multiple specialties and hospital sites.

🌍 Global Landscape

  • Today clinicians view chest CT scans, compare them with prior tests, and interpret new findings.
  • Tomorrow’s trillion‑dollar medical‑AI companies are expected to arise from three pillars: day‑to‑day clinician workflow systems, data that span the whole patient‑care journey, and foundational models that continuously add diagnostic capability.
  • Three global hubs illustrate this trajectory:
    • Pro Medicus (Melbourne, Australia) – imaging‑workflow software.
    • Tempus AI (Chicago, United States) – molecular diagnostics and patient‑data services.
    • Diagens Tech (Hangzhou, China) – large foundational models for medical imaging.

📊 Market Landscape

Company Location Primary Business Focus Market Capitalisation (8 Oct 2026)
Pro Medicus Melbourne, Australia Imaging software & workflow tools (Visage7) RMB 78 billion
Tempus AI Chicago, United States Molecular diagnostics and data services RMB 84 billion
Diagens Tech Hangzhou, China Medical‑imaging large foundational models RMB 22 billion

🧩 Diagens Tech’s Platform Strategy

  • Starts from a single, regulated use case and is now expanding to additional specialties and hospital sites.
  • Provides a unified foundation on which clinical specialists can build, deploy and operate thousands of custom models.
  • Positions the company to occupy the emerging third asset class in medical AI – models that generate new clinical capabilities continuously.

⚙️ How the Platform Evolves

  • As AI amplifies specialist expertise, medical‑imaging foundational models shift from standalone products to scalable platform assets.
  • The platform is designed to integrate with existing workflow systems, enabling hospitals to organise image reading, reporting and cross‑institutional collaboration around a single foundation.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Imaging accounts for roughly 80 % of global clinical data and supports about 14,000 indication‑specific tasks across modalities such as CT, MR, ultrasound, pathology and more.
  • With over 25 billion imaging scans performed worldwide each year, a platform that lets specialists rapidly create and run custom models promises faster, more specialized insights.
  • If workflows and data already command high valuations (as seen with Pro Medicus), foundational‑model platforms like Diagens Tech could become the next high‑value asset class in medical AI.

#MedicalAI #FoundationalModels #HealthcareTech

Source: Hangzhou Diagens Biotechnology Clinical Screens in Melbourne, Data in Chicago, Foundational Models in Hangzhou: Tracing Medical AI’s Trillion-Dollar Value

item.title: Utah AI Pilot Autonomously Renews Prescriptions Without Physician in Loop
item.description:
Utah AI Pilot Autonomously Renews Prescriptions Without Physician in Loop

On January 6, 2026 the Utah Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP) publicly launched Doctronic’s autonomous AI prescription pilot – the first known instance in the United States where an AI system renews medications without a physician directly involved.

🔍 Overview

  • The AI Prescription Pilot operates under Utah’s Artificial Intelligence Policy Act (Title 13, Chapter 72) as a regulatory “sandbox.”
  • The sandbox allows companies to test innovative AI products in the real world for a limited time, with temporary relief from specified state rules, but it does not waive federal law or provide a general license to practice medicine.
  • Participants sign a regulatory mitigation agreement negotiated by the OAIP with the relevant state agency; the agreement can waive or modify specified state enforcement but cannot grant a medical license.

🧩 How it works

Phase Process Current Status
Phase One A licensed physician must review and authorize every AI‑recommended prescription renewal before it is sent to a pharmacy. Ongoing – no medication group has reached Phase Two.
Phase Two The AI may submit approved renewals directly to the pharmacy; pharmacists retain authority to escalate to a Doctronic physician. Not yet activated – each medication group must independently reach 250 filled prescriptions before OAIP approval.
  • The AI can process 30‑, 60‑, or 90‑day renewals of existing prescriptions only.
  • It may not issue new prescriptions, handle controlled or addictive substances, or change treatment plans.
  • The pilot covers renewal of 191 medications for chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

📊 Performance (May 2026 OAIP report)

  • AI recommended renewal in 72 % of cases; the remaining 28 % were escalated to a physician.
  • Reviewing physicians agreed with 91 % of the AI’s renewal recommendations (rising to 97 % when a second physician’s opinion was considered).
  • Physicians judged 69 % of escalations to be warranted, labeling the rest as overly cautious.
  • The data were reported by Doctronic’s own physicians; the OAIP has launched an independent review.

🚨 Regulatory response

  • Utah’s Medical Licensing Board demanded immediate suspension of the pilot activities, even as the program continues beyond the pilot phase and Doctronic eyes expansion to other states.
  • The OAIP tightened Phase Two criteria: the original agreement allowed advancement after 250 total prescriptions were filled; the new rule requires each medication group to independently hit 250 filled prescriptions.
  • The underlying mitigation agreement runs for a 12‑month term (≈ Oct 2025 – Oct 2026). Extensions can be requested no later than 30 days before term end, with a maximum of two 12‑month extensions.
  • Participants must promptly report consumer harm, privacy breaches, or unauthorized data use, which could trigger removal from the program.
  • The sandbox does not resolve whether an AI system performing the clinical determination to renew a prescription constitutes the unlicensed practice of medicine under Utah Code § 58‑67‑301 and related statutes.

🌐 Future outlook

  • Doctronic is in active discussions with regulators in Arizona, Texas, and Wyoming about similar programs.
  • A second AI company, Legion Health, has signed an agreement with the OAIP for a renewal pilot limited to non‑controlled psychiatric medications; its demonstration period has not yet begun.
  • No medication group has yet moved the pilot into Phase Two, and the OAIP’s independent review is pending.
  • If extensions are granted, the pilot could continue through October 2027 or October 2028, subject to compliance with reporting and safety requirements.

#AIRegulation #MedicalAI #PrescriptionRenewal #UtahAI

Source: When AI Writes the Prescription: Licensure, Liability, and the Corporate Practice of Medicine in Utah’s Autonomous AI Pilot - Law Offices of Snell & Wilmer

item.title: International Study Evaluates 11 AI Systems for Gum Disease Diagnosis
item.description:
International Study Evaluates 11 AI Systems for Gum Disease Diagnosis

On October 5, 2026, an international study led by Dr. Yaniv Mayer, senior physician and director of the residency program in the Department of Periodontics and Implants at Rambam and senior lecturer at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Faculty of Medicine, was published in the Journal of Clinical Periodontology. The research examined, for the first time on a comparative basis, eleven leading artificial‑intelligence systems to see how they perform as auxiliary tools for diagnosing and treating gum disease.

🔍 Overview

  • The study compared 11 AI systems on their ability to diagnose gum diseases and recommend treatment.
  • It sought to determine which systems provide safer recommendations and which might endanger patients.
  • The work emphasizes that AI is becoming a working tool for professionals in fields such as medicine, where it can help achieve faster, more accurate, and more efficient diagnoses.

🦷 AI in Periodontics

  • Artificial intelligence is rapidly integrating into medical practice, including periodontics (gum health).
  • The study’s results highlight that expert oversight remains essential for safe patient care, even when AI tools are used.

📊 Study Details

  • Lead researcher: Dr. Yaniv Mayer (Senior physician, Department of Periodontics and Implants, Rambam; Senior lecturer, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Faculty of Medicine).
  • Publication: Journal of Clinical Periodontology.
  • Date: October 05, 2026.
  • Scope: Comparative evaluation of 11 leading AI systems for gum disease diagnosis and treatment recommendation.

💡 Why It Matters

  • The Technion has been Israel’s technological engine for more than 100 years, driving innovation, technology, and entrepreneurship.
  • By testing AI tools in dentistry, the study contributes to the broader effort of transforming ideas into impact across medicine and security.
  • Findings help clinicians understand the limits of AI, reinforcing the need for human expertise to ensure patient safety.

🚀 Looking Ahead

  • Continued collaboration between academic institutions (Technion, Rambam) and AI developers will shape how AI assists clinicians.
  • Ongoing research will be needed to refine AI recommendations and safeguard against potential risks.

Discover how AI performs in gum disease diagnosis and why expert oversight remains essential for safe patient care.

#AI #Periodontics #MedicalAI #Healthcare #Technion

Source: Can AI Safely Support Gum Disease Diagnosis?

item.title: Diagens Tech Unveils iMedImage Suite for Continuous Medical Imaging AI
item.description:
Diagens Tech Unveils iMedImage Suite for Continuous Medical Imaging AI

🔍 Overview

On Sept. 25, during the fifth Global Digital Trade Expo, Diagens Tech demonstrated how medical imaging data can drive AI‑enabled productivity. The company presented a four‑layer product suite that builds on its universal foundation model, iMedImage®, and showed more than 20 use cases across specialties such as obstetrics, cardiology, emergency care, and oncology.

🧩 Architecture

Layer Description
iMedImage® Large‑scale foundation model for medical imaging covering 43 organs/anatomical sites and 61 disease areas
iMedStudio™ Workspace for multimodal intelligent annotation, AI‑assisted image processing, expert review and quality control
iMedMaaS® Platform for training and deploying models for specific specialties
iMedLoop™ (includes DoctorBench®) Closed‑loop system linking data collaboration, evaluation, release and feedback

⚙️ How it works

  • Clinicians can participate in data annotation and correction through iMedStudio™, feeding professional expertise into ongoing model training.
  • iMedMaaS® trains specialty‑specific models on the foundation model’s knowledge.
  • iMedLoop™ continuously updates the production system, addressing the reality that clinical scenarios are neither standardized nor static.
  • AI AutoVision®, a karyotype‑assisted diagnostic software built on iMedImage®, has received Class III medical device registration from China’s NMPA.

📊 Key details

  • More than 3,000 professional annotators support the platform.
  • The underlying dataset contains 28.95 million medical imaging records.
  • The suite supports imaging modalities including CT, MRI, X‑ray, ultrasound, CTA and endoscopy.
  • Partnerships with 99 hospitals, including 65 Grade A tertiary hospitals.
  • Demonstrated >20 representative use cases spanning obstetrics & gynecology, growth & development, cardiovascular & cerebrovascular conditions, emergency & critical care, and oncology.

💡 Why it matters

Medical AI lacks a fixed set of standardized answers; clinicians may interpret the same scan differently, and new disease entities and diagnostic modalities constantly emerge. Diagens Tech’s closed‑loop workflow and customizable foundation model aim to keep AI tools up‑to‑date, allowing continuous, compliant model rebuilding as clinical knowledge evolves. This approach aligns with the view that future competition will focus on the ability to create tailored models efficiently and continuously.

#MedicalAI #FoundationModels #Healthcare #ImagingAI

Source: Hangzhou Diagens Biotechnology Silicon Valley “Godfather” Kevin Kelly: AI’s Core Asset Is the Ability to Keep Building New AI Systems

item.title: NVIDIA Introduces NV-Reason-CT for 3D Volumetric CT Analysis
item.description:
NVIDIA Introduces NV-Reason-CT for 3D Volumetric CT Analysis

NVIDIA has developed NV-Reason-CT, a vision language model (VLM) specifically designed for 3D CT analysis. This foundation model extends chain-of-thought reasoning to full volumetric CT scans to support the generation of structured diagnostic reports and multistep follow-up conversations.

🔍 Overview

NV-Reason-CT is an open research and development foundation model intended for researchers and developers to post-train for specialized CT analysis applications. It is not a cleared clinical product or an autonomous diagnostic system.

Key capabilities include:

  • Generating detailed structured diagnostic reports.
  • Emulating the internal thinking process of radiologists, including systematic examination of anatomical regions, surfacing findings, considering differential diagnoses, and articulating uncertainty.
  • Supporting multistep follow-up conversations where clinicians and researchers can request clarifications on differential diagnoses or probe the model’s reasoning.

🧩 How it works

NV-Reason-CT processes CT volumes as native 3D inputs rather than independent 2D slices. This approach allows the model to reconstruct anatomical context across three spatial dimensions, which is necessary for studies that can comprise 300–600 axial slices.

  • Architecture: The model combines a Qwen3.5-4B LLM with a 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder (Primus/Colipri).
  • 3D Encoding: The encoder, adapted from Primus 3D ViT and initialized with Colipri weights, processes CT volumes resampled to 192³ voxels at 2 mm isotropic resolution using non-overlapping 8x8x8 patch tokens. This results in a vision token context of 13,824 (24x24x24).
  • Spatial Integration: All vision tokens and their 3D grid coordinates are passed to the LLM. The LLM utilizes 3D MRoPE to account for the spatial inter-token relationships.
  • Training: Weights are retrained end-to-end using a large cohort of CT data featuring structured reports, reasoning traces, and internally designed multistep VQA.

⚙️ Key details

To guide and evaluate the model, the NVIDIA team curated a CT ontology covering 59 total abnormalities in a format mapping to clinical documentation workflows:

Region Number of Abnormalities Examples
Chest 30 Lung nodules, pneumothorax
Abdomen 29 Hepatic lesions, renal cysts

💡 Why it matters

NV-Reason-CT builds on the reasoning methodology of NV-Reason-CXR. That preceding model was validated in a multireader clinical study accepted at RSNA 2026, which confirmed that the approach maintained diagnostic accuracy while providing radiologist time savings.

#NVIDIA #MedicalAI #ComputerVision #CTAnalysis #VLM

Source: Introducing NV-Reason-CT Open 3D CT VLM for Radiologist Chain-of-Thought Reasoning | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: RMS-RSP Method Proposed to Improve Medical QA Robustness
item.description:
RMS-RSP Method Proposed to Improve Medical QA Robustness

Researchers have proposed root-mean-square Robustness-based Sample Prioritization (RMS-RSP), a method designed to identify high-quality supervision for medical question-answering datasets where high-quality rationales are often scarce, noisy, or costly to validate.

🧩 How it works

RMS-RSP functions by:

  • Perturbing hidden states specifically at rationale tokens.
  • Measuring the resulting shift in the margin between the gold answer and the best distractor.

⚙️ Key details

The method was tested using the following parameters:

  • Model: MedGemma-4B-IT
  • Datasets: Five medical QA datasets
  • Baselines: Three training seeds, ten budgeted non-RSP selectors, and an unbudgeted full-supervision reference

💡 Why it matters

While the method did not establish universal accuracy gains, it demonstrated specific impacts on model consistency:

  • Accuracy: Locked-budget accuracy averaged 60.61%, compared to 60.08% for Random, with a statistically resolved gain of +1.44 points only on AfriMed-QA.
  • Robustness: After three answer-option reorderings, RMS-RSP improved semantic consistency by 2.85 points and robust accuracy by 1.91 points on average across all five datasets.
  • Efficiency: Training on every pool rationale raised macro accuracy to 63.74%, but consumed 29–254 times more rationale tokens and did not uniformly improve robustness.

Findings suggest that rationale-local boundary sensitivity can identify supervision that improves invariance to semantically equivalent formatting changes.

#MedicalAI #MedGemma #MachineLearning #NLP

Source: Which Medical Questions Deserve Rationales? Perturbation-Sensitive Selection for Robust QA

item.title: FreNet introduces visual prior‑driven feature reconfiguration for lesion segmentation
item.description:
FreNet introduces visual prior‑driven feature reconfiguration for lesion segmentation

A new framework called FreNet has been introduced to improve medical lesion segmentation by applying visual priors and feature reconfiguration at both pixel and feature levels.

🔍 Overview

  • Lesion segmentation in medical images is critical for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.
  • Two major challenges hinder accurate segmentation: complex background interference and diverse lesion morphology.
  • Existing encoder‑decoder methods mainly focus on enhancing feature extraction or redesigning decoding strategies, but they lack early prior guidance and feature reconfiguration during the encoding stage.

🛠️ How it works

  • Pixel‑level reconfiguration is performed before the encoding stage to suppress background responses.
  • Feature‑level reconfiguration occurs throughout the encoding stage to better handle varied lesion shapes.
  • The overall pipeline combines these two stages to produce precise lesion masks.

⚙️ Key components

Module Function
Implicit Prior Neural Network (IPNN) Models a continuous spatial field and leverages visual prior from SAM to reconfigure the input image before encoding.
Dual‑domain Feature Reconfiguration (DFR) Progressively reconfigures backbone features during encoding.
Frequency Decoupling Module (FDM) Decouples backbone features in the frequency domain to enhance foreground‑background discriminability.
Spatial Localization Module (SLM) Relocates features spatially and improves spatial stability after frequency decoupling.

📊 Performance

  • Evaluated on 9 medical image segmentation benchmarks spanning three imaging modalities.
  • Demonstrates significant improvements over state‑of‑the‑art (SOTA) methods.
  • On the challenging ETIS dataset, FreNet achieves 5.0 % higher Dice score than the previous SOTA method and 7.2 % higher than SAM.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides early visual‑prior guidance, addressing background interference.
  • Introduces dual‑domain reconfiguration to cope with diverse lesion morphologies.
  • Offers a consistently higher segmentation accuracy across multiple modalities, supporting more reliable clinical decisions.

#MedicalAI #LesionSegmentation #FreNet #DeepLearning #ComputerVision

Source: Feature Reconfiguration With Visual Prior for Medical Lesion Segmentation

item.title: Research Identifies Impact of Human Interventions on Multi-Agent Medical System Accuracy
item.description:
Research Identifies Impact of Human Interventions on Multi-Agent Medical System Accuracy

New research into multi-agent medical systems has identified that human interventions at specific “fault points” significantly alter diagnostic accuracy. The study analyzed simulated doctor-patient conversations within the MedQA dataset to determine how external influences shift AI reasoning and performance outcomes.

🧩 How it works

Researchers defined fault points as the specific moments in AI agent conversations where reasoning is most vulnerable to external influence. By targeting these moments, the study measured how different types of interventions affected the system’s ability to reach an accurate diagnosis.

⚙️ Key details

The impact of human intervention varied based on the accuracy and nature of the guidance provided:

Intervention Type Effect on Diagnostic Accuracy
Correct intervention methods Improved accuracy by up to 40%
Incorrect or bias-related interventions Degraded performance by up to 6%

Beyond accuracy shifts, incorrect interventions also led to increased diagnostic drift and uncertainty.

💡 Why it matters

The study revealed that AI agents exhibit behavioral similarities to real-world clinical cognitive biases. These findings demonstrate that identifying and guiding fault points may provide a mechanism for improving diagnostic robustness in multi-agent medical systems. Specific observed behaviors included:

  • Premature closure
  • Susceptibility to misleading cues

#MedicalAI #AIAgents #ClinicalReasoning #MedQA #HealthcareTech

Source: Examining the Vulnerability of Multi-Agent Medical Systems to Human Interventions for Clinical Reasoning

item.title: AI Detects Heart Disease in Women Through Mammograms
item.description:
AI Detects Heart Disease in Women Through Mammograms

A new study suggests that artificial intelligence (AI) can identify heart disease in women by analysing mammogram images.

🔍 Overview

  • AI can detect heart disease in women using mammograms, study suggests.

⚙️ Key details

  • The capability is demonstrated in a research study.
  • It targets female patients.
  • The analysis is performed on existing mammogram scans.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a potential method for early heart disease detection in women.
  • Utilises imaging already performed for breast cancer screening, offering additional health insights without extra procedures.

#AI #Healthcare #WomenHealth #MedicalAI

Source: AI (artificial intelligence)
